gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-noto-sans-: Gappy, loud, letter by letter. Electroharmonix splits each word into separate characters, while Noto Sans Tangsa follows with wide, inviting round letters that keep a full page of text easy on the eye.
Electroharmonix breaks every word into spaced-out, commanding letters with generous open curves, and Noto Sans TC sits beneath it in a plain sans. Its outward-opening curves finish the job.
Electroharmonix cuts each word into single, open-handed letters with real presence. And Noto Sans Thaana, a sans-serif with wide channels into each counter, keeps paragraphs flowing without a snag.

Approachable, almost bubbly. Noto Sans Thai fills its lowercase like inflated glass beads, and set under the gapped, striking letters of Electroharmonix, that rounded softness is easily the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-noto-tradi: Split letters, sharp attitude. Electroharmonix is best at announcing a line with commanding gaps, while Noto Traditional Nushu, a sans-serif with broad pen strokes and bowls that fill the line, is best at quietly carrying the text.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-numans: Spaced-out and loud. Numans, a plain sans with an s whose ends hang far from the spine, gives Electroharmonix a modern, clean counterweight, and that open-tracked looseness is what the pair does best.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-orienta: Striking from the first glance. Orienta, a plain sans with breathing counters and little gap between cases, does the quiet work of reading, while Electroharmonix is better at splitting words into bold single letters.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-oxygen: Electroharmonix is all gapped-out letters and open-handed curves. And Oxygen, a sans with curves that never close and lowercase nearly matching its capitals, makes the pair's contemporary, clean quality the thing you notice.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-radio-cana: Commanding up top. Electroharmonix lets gaps split each word, then Radio Canada, a sans-serif with tall, full c, s and z and no pressure variation in its line, carries a page along smoothly.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-sarpanch: Electroharmonix breaks each word into striking single letters. Sarpanch, a sans-serif with a clearly open e and tight ascender spacing, gives the pair a contemporary, approachable quality that makes the contrast so easy to enjoy.
